edges.cite: Preschern, Fluent C (2022), 'Returning Data From C Functions' patterns
edges.note: Both return several related values; Aggregate returns one struct-by-value where Out-Parameters use multiple caller pointers.
The bundled struct is passed/returned by value, relying on copy semantics to hand back an independent snapshot.
Data flows through the out-pointer so the return value stays free to carry a status code.
An out-parameter typically writes into storage the caller allocated and owns.
Selecting behavior with a mode/flag argument is the data-driven alternative to passing function pointers.
A flag argument bakes variant selection into one entry point; Strategy externalizes it as interchangeable polymorphic objects.
Clients create by naming an abstract product plus a specification; the trader maps the spec to a concrete class ('creation by specification').

edges.cite: Baumer & Riehle, 'Product Trader', PLoPD 3 (1997), Related Patterns
edges.note: Both decouple clients from concrete product classes; Product Trader keys creation on a runtime spec rather than a fixed factory hierarchy.
A newByName/trader lookup is an alternative to hard-coded Factory Methods for instantiating an abstract product.
A smart constructor wraps a newtype and is exported instead of the raw constructor, so the type's invariant cannot be bypassed.
A smart constructor is the sole exported factory function for a type, adding validation/normalization on top of plain factory construction.
The smart constructor is where the class invariant assumed by later contracts is first established and guaranteed.
A violated precondition/invariant assertion aborts immediately at the offending boundary, the fail-fast discipline.
Preconditions are typically realized as guard clauses that check obligations at routine entry.

edges.cite: POSA2 (Schmidt, Stal, Rohnert, Buschmann, 2000), Extension Interface, Related Patterns
edges.note: Both let one object present multiple role-specific interfaces; Extension Interface is the interface-partitioning form of Role Object.
Extension Object (Gamma, PLoPD3) and Extension Interface address the same need (add capabilities via extra interfaces); pick one formulation.

edges.cite: POSA4 (Buschmann, Henney, Schmidt, 2007), Ch.12 Extension Interface / Explicit Interface
edges.note: Each role reachable from the root is itself an Explicit Interface type the client depends on.

edges.cite: POSA4 (2007), Ch.12 Introspective Interface; cf. COM IUnknown::QueryInterface
edges.note: Introspection lets a client discover which extension interfaces a component supports before requesting them.
A dedicated metadata-query interface is one more explicit, separately declared interface on the component.
A plugin host queries each plugin's introspective interface to learn its capabilities/config at load time.
Separated Interface refines the explicit-interface idea by placing the interface in a different package from its implementation.
DI depends on clients coding to an explicit interface type so any implementation can be injected.
Plugin links a class to an abstraction declared as a Separated Interface, chosen per deployment via config.
Plugin uses a Service Locator (a registry seeded by config) to resolve the configured implementation at runtime.
Plugin frameworks invoke init/activate/shutdown callbacks on each loaded plugin at defined lifecycle points.
A lifecycle callback is a callback the container invokes specifically at defined lifecycle transitions (inversion of control).
Component Configurator drives components through init()/suspend()/fini() lifecycle hooks as it (re)configures them.
DI containers call lifecycle hooks (post-construct after injection, pre-destroy before disposal) around the injected object.
A HAL is a wrapper facade whose encapsulated low-level detail is register/peripheral access rather than an OS API.
A HAL commonly presents one fixed facade API whose backend module is selected per target at build/link time.
The HAL sits above and delegates to per-peripheral device drivers, presenting a uniform interface over them.
It is a Facade whose implementation behind the fixed API is chosen per platform at compile/link time.
Both pick an implementation per deployment; the facade/backend binds at build/link time, Plugin binds at config/runtime.
Wrapper Facade applies Facade specifically to encapsulate low-level, non-portable system APIs behind a cohesive type-safe class.
C++ wrapper facades over handles (mutex, socket, file) tie acquire/release to object lifetime via RAII.

edges.cite: cppreference / isocpp FAQ, 'Static Initialization Order Fiasco'
edges.note: Both defeat the static-init-order fiasco: Nifty Counter guards a shared static across TUs; Construct-On-First-Use hides it in a function-local static.

edges.cite: Meyers, Effective C++ 3rd ed, Item 4 (Meyers Singleton)
edges.note: A function returning a reference to a function-local static is the idiomatic C++ realization of a lazily-created Singleton.

edges.cite: Meyers & Alexandrescu, 'C++ and the Perils of Double-Checked Locking' (2004)
edges.note: Both give thread-safe lazy initialization; C++11 function-local statics supersede hand-written DCL for singletons.
The per-TU counter increments on first inclusion and decrements on last, reference-counting translation units to bound a static's lifetime.

edges.cite: Gamma et al., GoF, Iterator (internal vs external iterator)
edges.note: Enumeration Method is the internal iterator: the collection drives the loop, versus GoF Iterator's client-driven external cursor.

edges.cite: Gamma et al., GoF, Iterator (internal iterator supplies an operation to apply per element)
edges.note: The owner applies a client-supplied callback to each element internally instead of exposing a cursor.
Both replace repeated single-element calls: Batch Method moves a whole set per call; Enumeration Method loops internally over one callback.
Sibling coarse-grained interface methods that cut call/round-trip count; often applied together on the same API.
Fusing a check-then-act sequence into one method closes the inter-call race window a thread-safe interface must otherwise guard.
A fluent interface is a primary technique for giving an internal DSL its flowing host-language syntax.
Expression Builder layers the DSL's fluent grammar over a plain command-query API to keep the model clean.
C++ EDSLs are frequently implemented with expression templates so DSL expressions compile into efficient operations.
A static factory can return cached/shared instances instead of new ones, enabling instance control and flyweighting.
Both replace telescoping public constructors; static factories suit few params, Builder suits many optional ones.

edges.cite: Bloch, Effective Java, Item 1 (instance control) & Item 3
edges.note: A Singleton's getInstance() is a static factory; the factory's instance control is exactly what enforces the single instance.

edges.cite: Dave Cheney, 'Functional options for friendly APIs' (2014)
edges.note: Both configure objects with many optional params; functional options use composable option functions instead of a builder object.
Both name optional arguments to avoid long positional lists; one via variadic option functions, the other via chained setters on a proxy.
Each option is a first-class function/closure that mutates the value being configured, so options compose and default cleanly.
A retained-mode GUI keeps a persistent widget tree / scene graph the client mutates and the library redraws from.
